questions.prompt: A refactor touched eight files, the tests fail, and each fix makes the next failure worse. What is the right move?
options: Keep debugging forward until the tests pass
Rewind to the checkpoint from before the refactor and start over from a known-good state
Commit the broken state and move on
questions.explanation: Many steps have gone wrong at once, which is exactly the case for rolling back to a known-good checkpoint. Option A is the default mistake the lesson exists to fix. Option C empties the conversation but does not restore the files you broke. Option D banks the damage.

questions.prompt: A single typo in one config file needs fixing. Rewind, or edit directly?
options: Edit directly — one wrong thing in one file is not the rewind case
Rewind to before the session started
questions.explanation: The rewind threshold is more than one thing to undo; a single line is faster to fix in place. Option A is tempting as the cautious choice, but rewinding also costs the conversation around it. Option C throws away far more than the typo. Option D redoes work that was never broken.

questions.prompt: You deleted a file in Finder, outside Claude Code. You then rewind. Is the file back?
options: Yes — rewind restores the whole machine
Only if the tool itself snapshotted that file; rewinds restore the tool's session state, not changes made outside it
Yes, but only if you were in plan mode
Yes — rewind restores anything on disk from that time
questions.explanation: A rewind restores what the tool saw and changed, so a change made outside its view is not in any checkpoint. Option A is the tempting overestimate of what undo means. Option C invents a link between plan mode and file recovery. Option D claims a whole-disk rollback the mechanism does not provide.

questions.prompt: The conversation has grown long and full of dead ends, but the files are all fine. What do you reach for?
options: `/clear` — rewind restores state, it does not trim the conversation
questions.explanation: When the problem is conversation length rather than broken files, `/clear` is the trimming tool and rewind is the wrong one. Option A is the tempting mix-up: rewind restores state to a checkpoint, it does not shrink the conversation. Option C ignores that dead ends keep costing room. Option D would restore files that were never wrong and still leave the chat long.
